To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gradient descent is an effective method for optimizing high-dimensional Gaussian random field loss functions, and the distribution of the loss function after one step of gradient descent is close to normal with mean and variance depending on the curvature of the landscape.

1) the improved loss function obtained from a single step of gradient descent in a Gaussian random field has a distribution with a non-trivial covariance structure that is not Gaussian; 2) this distribution is well approximated by a Gaussian with the same mean but a different variance, which can be estimated by a simple formula; 3) the distribution of the global minimum in a Gaussian random fields is well approximated, in the limit of large dimension, by the Euler characteristic of the excursion set
the loss function of a high-dimensional optimization problem can be modelled by a Gaussian random fields, and that gradient descent in such a landscape is well understood.

Gaussian random field landscapes can be a useful tool in the study of high-dimensional optimisation problems, and in particular deep neural network training.
the Gaussian random field model is a useful toy model to study high-dimensional optimisation problems in deep learning.
